newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada plans share issue.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada plans share issue.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Monday it planned to issue up to 23 million ordinary shares in an offering that would partially fund its proposed hostile takeover of Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc.

Gulf said it filed a preliminary prospectus in Canada and a registration statement in the United States covering the sale 20 million ordinary shares plus another three million if the underwriters' over-allotment option is exercised.
The offering would be made in Canada and the United States, it said.
Underwriters for the offering include Goldman, Sachs & Co, RBC Dominion Securities Inc, Salomon Brothers Inc and TD Securities Inc.

Proceeds from the issue, which at Gulf's current share price would be above C$200 million, together with borrowings under a credit facility were to be used to pay for the C$1.3 billion Clyde acquisition.
Gulf said that if its Clyde offer was not successful, it would use net proceeds to fund a portion of its 1997 capital program and for other corporate purposes.

Gulf, which currently has 245 million shares outstanding, said A&G Resources Corp and investors led by Torch Energy Advisors Inc owned about 45 percent of the company and the public float comprised about 55 percent.
On a proforma basis, assuming all registered shares excluding the underwriters' over-allotment were sold, the public holdings would increase to about 58 percent, it said.
Gulf said when it launched its Clyde bid on December 18 that it arranged a credit facility with the Bank of Montreal to fund the deal, and would embark on a series of moves to pay off the debt.
The share issue, as well as sales of Canadian oil and gas properties and an initial public offering of a portion of its Indonesia subsidiary, were cited as moves planned.
Gulf shares, which earlier on Monday hit an all-time C$10.35 in Toronto, fell to C$9.85 following the share issue announcement.
